Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected plant debris. Apply copper-based bactericide. Avoid overhead watering and working in wet fields.

Pepper__bell___healthy.description: No disease detected — leaf appears healthy.
Pepper__bell___healthy.treatment: Continue regular monitoring and standard care.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease causing concentric ring spots on older leaves, starting from the bottom of the plant.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves. Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or copper-based). Rotate crops yearly.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Aggressive fungal disease that can destroy a potato crop within days in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply fungicide preventively. Destroy infected plants immediately. Ensure good field drainage.

Potato___healthy.description: No disease detected — leaf appears healthy.
Potato___healthy.treatment: Continue regular monitoring and standard care.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves and fruit.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.treatment: Use copper-based bactericides. Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove and destroy infected plant material.

Tomato_Early_blight.description: Fungal disease causing concentric ring spots (target-like pattern) on older, lower leaves.
Tomato_Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves. Apply fungicide. Mulch to prevent soil splash onto leaves.

Tomato_Late_blight.description: Fast-spreading fungal disease causing dark, water-soaked lesions, especially in cool, wet weather.
Tomato_Late_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Apply fungicide preventively. Improve air circulation.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease causing pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with olive-green mold underneath.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.treatment: Improve greenhouse/field ventilation to reduce humidity. Apply fungicide. Remove infected leaves.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Fungal disease causing small circular spots with dark borders and light centers, mainly on lower leaves.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves promptly. Apply fungicide. Avoid overhead watering.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.description: Pest damage from tiny mites causing stippled, discolored leaves and fine webbing.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.treatment: Apply miticide or insecticidal soap. Increase humidity around plants, as mites thrive in dry conditions.

Tomato__Target_Spot.description: Fungal disease causing brown lesions with concentric rings, resembling a target pattern.
Tomato__Target_Spot.treatment: Apply fungicide. Remove infected debris. Improve air circulation between plants.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.description: Viral disease spread by whiteflies, causing upward leaf curling and yellowing.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.treatment: Control whitefly populations with insecticide or sticky traps. Remove and destroy infected plants. No cure once infected.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Viral disease causing mottled light/dark green patterns on leaves and stunted growth.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants. Disinfect tools between plants. No chemical cure — prevention is key.

Tomato_healthy.description: No disease detected — leaf appears healthy.
Tomato_healthy.treatment: Continue regular monitoring and standard care.
